clue.text: Fitting for primate to retain one in office

indicators.note: to retain means to hold something within, so the primate wraps around what follows

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: in tells us the word for one sits inside the word for office

parts.note: a post is a job or office
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A comment about whether it suits an archbishop to keep a colleague in a position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an archbishop, the usual surface sense, but here it is the animal. 'in' and 'to retain' are two separate container signals, one nested inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apposite is apt or well suited to the occasion.

clue.text: Proceedings in a court get no-one's backing

indicators.note: backing means the letters for no-one are read from the end to the start

parts.note: no-one split as NO and ONE, with one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Nobody supports someone's legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-one' is split into its two parts, the second being the Roman numeral, and 'backing' turns the pair round to give ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a set of proceedings brought before a court.

clue.text: Dainty little Parisian quartet

parts.note: petit is French for little, as a Parisian would say it
a quartet is a group of four

explanation.surface: Describes a delicate group of four musicians from Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dainty' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun here: a dainty is a small delicacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fancy cake served with coffee is a dainty, a small sweet treat.

clue.text: Waiter finds a way to serve salmi for starters

parts.note: a salmi is a game ragout, so serving it as a first course means serving a stew
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A waiter works out how to bring a game dish to the table as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts the 'a way' piece first, but the stew piece leads the answer; 'finds' and 'to' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward serves food and drink to passengers, as a waiter does at table.

clue.text: Follow development of middle-eastern marathon?

indicators.note: middle- picks out the central letter of the word it is joined to

parts.note: a marathon is a long running race; the question mark marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A question about the growth of a long-distance run in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle-eastern' looks like a place, but it gives the middle letter of 'eastern', T.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace something is to track its history or course step by step.

clue.text: Seaside frolic makes headlines

explanation.surface: A day at the beach turns into news.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing in the waves at the beach is a splash about; a newspaper splash is a big front-page story with large headlines.

clue.text: Our pal's become very difficult

indicators.note: become says the letters of the words before it change into a new form

explanation.surface: Our friend has fallen on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 'pal's' is 'pal has', so its S counts; 'become' rearranges OUR PALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlous is an old word for dangerous or precarious, a situation full of trouble.

clue.text: Dressing made from tip-top blended oil

parts.note: tip-top means first-rate, A1, written with the letter I for the figure 1

indicators.note: blended means the letters of oil are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A salad dressing made from the best blended oil.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a British way of saying first-class; crosswords often read the figure 1 as the letter I. 'blended' gives OLI from the oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic mayonnaise from Provence, used as a sauce or dressing.

clue.text: Dire result of leaving German in German city

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for German sits inside the city name

parts.note: Hanover is a city in Germany

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a German in a German city, with grim results.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read loosely: the grim morning after you finally leave the party. HANOVER is a city in Lower Saxony.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning headache after heavy drinking is a nasty after-effect.

clue.text: Reportedly, they steal underwear

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: people who nick, or steal, are nickers

explanation.surface: A claim that some people are thieves of underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is British slang for steal, so thieves are nickers; the knickers' silent K makes it sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's pants, a type of underwear.

clue.text: Ideally suited to country-house life, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the phrase is spoken, sounding like another

parts.note: someone born to life in a country house is born to the manor

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be a natural for the life of the landed gentry.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like 'to the manor born', which was also a British TV sitcom about a woman who loses her country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Born to a way of doing things, so naturally fitted for a role or situation.

clue.text: Stare down when not in front

parts.note: if you are not in, you are out
the face of a building is its front

explanation.surface: Advice on staring someone out when you are not at the head of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To outface someone is to defeat them by holding their gaze or by boldness.

clue.text: Rich zoo ordered Spanish fare

indicators.note: ordered here means put in a new order, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A wealthy zoo has put in an order for Spanish food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like placing an order for food, but it signals the rearrangement of RICH ZOO.
explanation.definitionFit: Spicy paprika-flavoured pork sausage, a staple food of Spain.

clue.text: Make summaries for jailbird of little brain

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a jailbird
someone of little brain is dense or slow-witted

explanation.surface: An unintelligent prisoner is given the job of writing précis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a text is to shorten it, which is what writing summaries does.

clue.text: Case where head's agony is revealed

parts.note: nut is slang for head, with the possessive S
hell is extreme suffering or agony

explanation.surface: A medical scenario in which a headache is diagnosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' sounds medical, but it is a shell or casing.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard shell around a nut's kernel is its casing.

clue.text: Urbane girl carries a small volume

indicators.note: carries means holds within, so the girl's name goes around the other pieces

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: A sophisticated young woman has a little book with her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts A and V inside SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Suave means smoothly polite and sophisticated in manner.

clue.text: Native wants old clothing popular in Lincoln

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces before it sit inside the president's nickname

parts.note: Abe is the nickname of US President Abraham Lincoln
rig is informal for an outfit of clothing
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: An indigenous person wants to see vintage garments popular in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' could be the English city, but it is Abe Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aborigine is an original inhabitant of a land, especially Australia.

clue.text: Attlee's accepted a note from climber

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the nickname holds the next pieces

parts.note: Clement Attlee, the post-war British Prime Minister, was known as Clem, with the possessive S
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The British Prime Minister Attlee took a note from a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer but it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a woody plant that grows up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Bigwigs from the MCC

explanation.surface: Important men from the cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: The MCC (Marylebone Cricket Club) owns Lord's, the London cricket ground, so the place stands for the club.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers and nobles are grandees; the MCC's headquarters and ground in London is called Lord's.

clue.text: Cloth-worker from south London suburb

parts.note: Pinner is a suburb in north-west London

explanation.surface: A textile worker comes from somewhere in the south of London.
explanation.walkthrough: PINNER is a suburb in the London borough of Harrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinner turns fibre into yarn for weaving cloth.

clue.text: He leaves money to inspect a rubbish-tip

parts.note: to test something is to examine or inspect it

indicators.note: tip means tilt over, so the word for rubbish is turned end to end

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A man leaves cash to look over a refuse dump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish-tip' looks like a dump, but 'tip' turns ROT into TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is a person who makes a will, so bequeaths money and property.

clue.text: Largely a result of hay fever, say

indicators.note: a result of signals the letters come out of the word before rearranged

explanation.surface: Most sneezing is caused by pollen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' looks like a qualifier but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Hay fever is one example of a bodily overreaction to a substance such as pollen.

clue.text: Rib apprentice for getting prickly plant

parts.note: to rib is to tease or make fun of
an apprentice is a learner, L as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Joking at a trainee's expense for buying a thorny plant.
explanation.walkthrough: L plates mark a learner driver in Britain, so L stands for any learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A teasel is a tall plant with spiny flower heads once used for raising nap on cloth.

clue.text: Sentimental parent has desire to embrace sovereign

parts.note: ma is a mother, a parent

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug or enclose, so the desire wraps round the king

parts.note: a wish is a desire
K stands for king, a sovereign

explanation.surface: A soppy mother longs to hug a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' could be a gold coin, but here it is a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly or excessively sentimental.

clue.text: Excite some sarawak engineers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some engineers in Sarawak, Borneo, can be stirred up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse or stir is to excite, the sense of to waken.

clue.text: Father pocketed old German cross

indicators.note: pocketed means put away inside, so the word for father holds the other piece

parts.note: a sire is a father
alt is German for old

explanation.surface: A father has taken an elderly German's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old German' is not a person but the German word for old.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross, as on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: Fur leading buyer sold at discount?

indicators.note: something sold at an event is in it, so the buyer's letter is put inside the sale

parts.note: a sale is a time of discounted prices; the question mark flags the loose sense

indicators.note: leading means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A fur bought by the main customer at a reduced price.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter of 'buyer', B, goes inside SALE, the discount event it is 'sold at'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the dark costly pelt of a small marten from Siberia.

clue.text: Acting presumptuously by removing basic rights

explanation.surface: Someone behaving with cheek by stripping others of their freedoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking liberties is behaving too familiarly; literally, it is taking freedoms away from people.

clue.text: Ridiculous reason for introducing Castilian lady

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests something absurd, so the word reason is jumbled

explanation.surface: An absurd excuse for introducing a woman from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for introducing' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Señora is the Spanish title for a married woman, used in Castile.

clue.text: OK is hardly descriptive of such health

definitions.text: is hardly descriptive of such health

explanation.surface: A remark that 'OK' is a poor word for good health.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is cryptic: health that is just 'OK' is far from being described as very well, yet the phrase itself means OK.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying very well is agreeing, like saying all right; being in excellent health is being very well.
